newsitem.title: USA: Dow stalls in bid to set new record closing high.
newsitem.headline: Dow stalls in bid to set new record closing high.

text.p: The Dow industrials stalled in their bid to snare a new record close as late selling cut gains, but the broader market remained solidly higher as a tame wholesale inflation report further calmed rate fears.

"Core producer prices were down a little bit and jobless claims were up. Now people are more sanguine about the (September 24) FOMC meeting. Some are thinking the Fed won't do anything and the stock market is moving ahead," said Hildegard Zagorski, a Prudential Securities market analyst.
The Dow rose 17 to about 5772, off the day's high 5794.13.
The blue chip index settled just shy of May 22's record closing high of 5778.00.

The Nasdaq Composite surged 12 points or 1.03 percent to about 1166, still far from its record closing high of 1249.15 set June 5. The S&P 500 rose four to about 671, nearing its May 24 record closing peak of 678.51.
Winners beat losers 7-4 on heavy NYSE volume of about 399 million shares. It was the most active NYSE trading session since August 2's 442 million.
Stocks continued to bolt higher as the long bond yield edged lower. The long bond rose 13/32 to yield 7.08 percent.

Although August producer prices rose a sharper-than-expected 0.3 percent, the closely watched core rate excluding the volatile food and energy components fell 0.1 percent against expectations for a 0.1 percent rise.
Weekly jobless claims rose to 338,000 for the week ended Sept. 7, above private economists' expectations of 329,000.
On Friday, consumer prices are due out. The core and overall rates were forecast up 0.2 percent. August's retail sales report is seen rising 0.7 percent.
Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany, noted Thursday's stock rally was broad-based.

"There's a good story here for economically sensitive stocks and a good story for consumer growth stocks. That happens only when investors believe that it will be a Goldilocks economy -- not too hot or too cold," he said.

But Johnson believes the PPI report and Wednesday's Federal Reserve Beige Book "makes the odds good that the Fed will raise rates 25 basis points at its Sept 24 meeting. What that means is the odds the economy will slow to a more sustainable pace (are) getting better and better and better."
"In a way, again we've engineered a soft landing. We'd be looking at a perfect world," Johnson added.

Alfred Goldman, technical research director at A.G. Edwards & Sons, was impressed by the day's market action. "There's a normal magnetism of a new high. But this market has had a number of tests and passed the exams. It shows the dominant mood is one of wanting to own stocks."
Zagorski noted Nasdaq's surge was aided by Microsoft, which rose 3-1/2 to 128-5/8. Microsft outlined an aggressive rollout of several new Internet-based products and services.
Among other issues, Duracell jumped 9-7/8 to 58-1/4 and Gillette added one to 66 after the companies agreed to merge in a $7 billion stock-swap deal.

Xerox fell three to 54-7/8. Xerox and Kohlberg Kravis Roberts ended a pact to sell Xerox's Talegen Holdings insurance businesses to a group of investors led by KKR for $2.7 billion. Smith Barney and Cowen downgraded Xerox.
Motorola extended its losses, off 1-1/4 to 47-3/4. Goldman and Bear Stearns downgraded the stock. Motorola fell 1-5/8 Wednesday after warning of a shortfall in quarterly results.

Energy stocks gave up some of their recent gains. Smith Barney downgraded the group to underweight from overweight. Anadarko Petroleum fell 3/4 to 54-1/8 and Louisiana Land & Exploration fell 2-3/8 to 56.
Among the Dow oil components, Texaco lost 7/8 to 93-3/4, Exxon rose 1/4 to 85 and Chevron was unchanged at 61-1/2.

U.S. Robotics rose 4-7/8 to 61-3/4 as expectations grew that the company would have a faster modem on the market by the end of the year. The company would not commment on whether it is close to shipping a 56 kilobits bits per second modem.
Brooktrout Technology climbed 5-1/4 to 31-1/2 after forecasting third-quarter revenues and profits will exceed analysts' expectations.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 11.86 to 1165.81.
The S&P 500 index rose 3.85 to 671.13.
(Figures official as of 1645 EDT/2045 GMT)
-- Wall Street desk, 212 859 1721
